TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Rat: Luc(6) Nik(4) Eld(2) 4/16/2026 4:44 AM Rebuild for Lady perchta 4:46 AM Name: Nikola Ancestry: Awakened animal Heritage: swimming animal Class: enigma bard - cosmos oracle Age: 19 Backstory: Nikola was originally born in a natural preserve in arctic waters, he spent his days as a pup as any otter would, never straying too far from his mother, learning to swim and eventually how to use simple tools slightly faster than his siblings did. As he grew he began to dive for his food along with the rest of his family, and also began to form more connections with his siblings as he was old enough to play with them often and desired to do so. In early adulthood he continued his usual lifestyle until one day where he met a pale white otter, she was like nothing he had seen, in fact he was a little frightened when he met her but that quickly changed when he noticed she seemed sad and seemingly had no other otters to play with, he approached her and tried to play, to which she was initially dismissive but eventually joined. A few years later into adulthood she had 2 kits newly born, the night of, Nikola was floating looking up at the sky staring at the stars appreciating his life, as he saw the stars he looked deeper, into the sky, into the cosmos, past the stars into a place an intelligent life would have assumed was empty, but it wasn’t, he saw a being that conveyed to him with that single glance that drew his vision the knowledge a feeling a dread and insignificance he had never felt before. He had never felt anything close to existentialism in his life, but his feeling in this glance bore such unbearable futility, it was beyond existentialism in itself. He screamed, he cried, he grit his teeth, he pawed at his face, until his mind gave and he passed out. 4:46 AM When Nikola awoke, he felt different, shaken still but unable to grasp fully at the memory of what he had witnessed in his reflection on the water he noticed a marking like that of an 8 pointed star on his forehead, he was almost sure that it had not been there before, Then he noticed something else, the way he viewed the world everything made a bit more sense, concepts he wasn’t able to conceptualise before now felt like second nature. He knew languages he had not known, he could speak with chords he did not have, as he looked at his love and his pups he understood that their minds were not that of his own, he felt a sense of morality in his mind that told him that he needed to protect their existence, futile as it may be, this conflicted with another feeling a desire to figure out more about this fresh world he had been placed in. As he thought about his actions the next few days, he noticed how his family was acting differently towards him, that they could tell he was not the same as he was, this realisation brought him to tears, and he left. He found a researcher out in the reserve and went up to them, talked to them, struck a deal, they could research what had happened to him and he would help work at the preserve and keep his family unmeddled with from a distance. He worked here for a little over a decade, until one day, he was sweeping his living quarters when he scratched his forehead and as he did he saw a memory of the vision he saw, he once more felt his consciousness fleeting but this time when he awoke he found himself in a new place, all together. After he did his best to come to terms with the fact he had no way home, he found a new purpose. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Mime [Nysra 8|Dodo 10|Gerb 3] 4/19/2026 5:23 PM Name : Samalyss Ancestry : Nymph Heritage : Slimeheart Class : Ruffian Rogue / School of Mentalism Wizard Age : 32 Once upon a grove within the First World, there existed a dryad bound to a slumbering tree. His purpose was simple. Guard the tree, guide others away from it, and let it sleep in peace. He never asked why and simply followed what he had been ordered. He did his job well, though with the usual fey twist. Lulling others into traps, misleading them onto more dangerous paths, and cackling loudly whenever his pranks were sprung successfully. Those were always the best parts of his duty. Every few days he made preparations for the next week's schemes by going deep into the forest and gathering more resources, but this week's plans were interrupted by a cluster of strange floating lights. They circled him briefly before drifting away from the forest, leading him deeper within. Confident in his remaining defenses, he chose to follow, trusting that nothing would threaten his tree in his absence. Shuffling through the brush, he came upon a group of mindless oozes pummeling their prey then gathering to devour it. Another helpless beast stumbled into their reach, panicking as it dodged their pseudopods until one finally struck. Yet the creature did not fall. It vanished away with arcane light. The nymph slammed his fist into the earth as he laughed at the oozes for falling for one of his oldest tricks, unaware there was another just behind him. His laughter died down as he turned, only to be met with an ooze lashing toward his face, and then he too disappeared. His laughter echoed from far above. For he was hanging safely within his tree the entire time, hurling illusions and still cackling at his own tricks. 5:23 PM His laughter was quickly interrupted as the tree began to shake. It groaned, uprooting itself as it rose and shook the nymph and its leaves off its branches. The ancient tree grew tired as it had cared not for a guardian, and yearned only to slumber in peace, before a sharp branch sliced the nymph in half and flung him away. Samalyss managed to halt himself. He slumped over only to notice the oozes he previously mocked slowly gather toward him. All of his pranks had finally caught up to him, and he could not help but laugh at the irony, unaware that he was being plucked away into the convergence. A few moments passed and Samalyss opened his eyes, he found himself in a strange new realm. He rose and wobbled back and forth. He looked down, only to find that his lower half had been reborn with the ooze he once mocked. An eternal reminder of his demise. But he did not despair. If anything, he laughed. For he had enjoyed every moment of it and learned little from his mistakes. With a new getup and a second chance he's ready to perform a spectacular encore to rise into becoming the greatest trickster Axiom had ever seen! In the summer they’d hunt game in the alpine tundra, fish lakes and rivers fed by snowmelt, and forage for valuable medicinal herbs difficult to access for most communities. Hjalmar often found himself at the forefront of many hunts, using his connection to earth, water and ice to guide and support his fellow tribesfolk. As more of his smaller kin found themselves wounded in the hunt, Hjalmar found himself more frequently jumping into the frey to protect them. Between his armor, his powers, and his enthusiasm to risk his own life for the sake of others, he soon became one of the tribe’s most trusted defenders. On the other, himself and this creature of frost and fury. The reality-shattering event left deep marks on Hjalmar’s spirit, imbuing him with some of the latent spiritual power of the Convergence, which he is still unused to even to this day. When the avalanche and earthquake settled, Hjalmar found himself in a wild land unlike anything he’d experienced before. He was not far from a town he’d soon come to know as Bramblecove. Nearby, he could see a group of scaly traders traveling by a boat amongst the trees. Unfortunately for them, the elemental, too, had been transported in the Convergence. Its rage now redoubled by being ripped from its home, it continued its rampage, with a host of fresh prey to set itself upon. Hjalmar managed to slay the monster, saving the traders. He soon forged a strong bond with them, despite how alien they seemed to someone so used to snow and sea. In return for saving their lives, the traders took Hjalmar in, bringing him into Bramblecove, teaching him what they knew of the Convergence and the Verdant Expanse, and introducing him to local adventurers. They were the ones who encouraged him to travel to Axiom, in the hopes that he might find new purpose and better come to understand his powers there. He also, quietly, hopes to find a newfound family to fill the void left by his lost tribe. Thus he will throw himself into harm's way to protect his fellow adventurers in the pursuit of a new home. Kobold! (edited) 12:14 PM Backstory: Dr. Mordaine Catalys was known in his world for his achievements. A true polymath, he dabbled in medicine, mathematics, physics, engineering and chemistry. Despite his growing fame he lived a lonely life. His connections were peers and co-workers, not friends. Most of his time was spent in his laboratory. When he was approached by a wealthy noble to create a portal to another world he jumped at the opportunity. After many years of experiments his team succeeded in the making of the very first Voltrift generator. The contraption took up most of the space in the largest room of the laboratory. Aether condensers powered by tesla coils. Phase injectors to twist the fabric of space and time. Resonant stabilizers to keep the event horizon stable. Each of the grand contraption’s parts was someone’s life’s work. But for all of the team’s scientific knowledge, none of them were experienced in real life scenarios. They never stopped to ask whether they should build this machine instead of asking whether they could. And worst of all, they missed all of the signals their mysterious patron was giving off. The first time the Voltrift generator was activated, they all celebrated. But their patron did not join them. Instead he moved to the control console and started adjusting settings like a man possessed. The man had never shown true skill in the sciences, despite his deep interest. By the time Mordaine noticed what he was doing, he had completed his task. The open rift shifted to show another world, a dark, shattered place, ravaged by entropic energies. Waiting on the other side of the rift was a creature unlike Mordaine had ever seen. (edited) 12:14 PM The creature stepped through the portal but seemed to flicker as if reality itself rejected its presence. The otherworldly entropic energy that laid waste to the other world followed in its footsteps. It flowed through the creature’s flesh, making its form shift. It took the shape of several tendrils of energy and pierced through each of the scientists and their patron, lifting them from the ground. Mordaine felt a connection form, a metaphysical link to the creature. He felt as if he was being disconnected from the world around him, his senses shutting down one by one. Desperately he reached for the Flux regulator and set the tesla coils powering the Voltrift generator to maximum output. The entire room was now overloaded with energy. Arcs of lightning rampaged through the laboratory tearing it apart and damaging the machinery. The portal grew unstable and winked out of existence. The creature’s flickering grew more chaotic as this happened until it disappeared. The scientists had survived, but their patron had not. The enigmatic man had been struck by the arcs of lightning and was now a burned heap of flesh. The scientists were traumatized by the experience. Some recovered, while others left the circles of scientific development. More concerningly, some of them grew mad, claiming they sometimes saw the creature, stalking them. 12:14 PM It was only when a few of them were found dead that Mordaine took them seriously. He volunteered to perform the autopsies himself and discovered that each of them had missing organs or body parts, cut cleanly from them, too cleanly to be the work of a blade. At this point Mordaine started seeing it too, the creature stalking him in the shadows and disappearing without a trace. His worst fear was realized when the creature attacked him, biting through his wrist and leaving only a smooth stump. The creature immediately flickered out of existence leaving him bleeding and screaming in pain. As he worked to cauterize the wound, what he found was not a wound torn by teeth, but a smooth surface as if contact with the creature had deleted his hand from existence. For the next few years the same thing kept happening. The other scientists found dead with similar injuries, and consecutive attacks by the creature. Each time he lost a part of himself to it. An ear, a foot, the left side of his torso. Yet Mordaine struggled to live, replacing each body part with metallic parts. He studied the creature and discovered that it had linked itself to the scientists. It was stealing their existence in this world, so that it would be allowed to exist in turn. Mordaine also realized that the creature could not travel to other worlds through its own power. With no way of defeating it, he thought to evade it, and prevent it from stealing the existence it needed. He built another Voltrift generator and activated it. By this point Mordaine only had his brain and heart left, the rest of his body now a marvel of technology, powered by steam and electricity. All of the other scientists were long dead, having failed to avoid the creature’s short but violent attacks. 12:15 PM Perhaps the creature sensed what he was doing, or somehow learned of his plan. It attacked him before he could step through the portal to a different world, not the one the creature originated from. But Mordaine had a contingency, he lured the creature to the portal and as both of them were between worlds he set off an explosive. The Voltrift generator exploded and the portal destabilized. Both of them were flung through reality in opposite directions. Thousands of worlds passed through Mordaine’s vision as he was propelled in the space between them. He clashed with other versions of himself...or perhaps the same version, but from a different time. This took a toll on his mind. Although he kept his identity, it was at the cost of much of his great scientific knowledge. However something about this process stabilized his being and aligned it with Ao. He crashed through the walls of reality and into this new world. Here he would make a new life for himself under the name Catalyst, selling alchemical wares and medical expertise (grafts and tattoos in the future) while adventuring through the gates to learn more about the universe, and hopefully discover a means to destroy the creature if it ever finds him again. Born solely to fulfill a contract made with a devil by her parents, exchanging her life in order to revive their deceased daughter, Elthara’s soul was tainted with an infernal mark she didn’t know she had within her until she reached adulthood and her body and psyche started to change to fit her new nature. Incapable of recognizing herself in the mirror with her new appearance and stripped of her “weakening” emotions like empathy or regret, a new version of Elthara who had been overtaken by her infernal nature was born, and when that happened, the devil came to claim her as his new underling responsible for gathering souls under his name. With a new purpose to fulfill, Elthara found a twisted joy in gathering desperate people’s souls through betting games and deals, experiencing a strong feeling of pride when she got to defeat her opponents through sheer luck or by cheating when things didn’t look in her favor, and with the passage of the years, that pride turned into arrogance. Acting increasingly carelessly, blindly trusting in her capability to outskill her opponent or cheat through any bet, eventually Elthara started letting her opponents choose the nature of the bet, and that blind pride would be her downfall when one day she got challenged by a Nephilim working for another devil into a drinking game, which she gladly accepted. To Elthara’s disgrace, she lost before an opponent that was better than her in every possible sense, irreparably damaging her ego, and to add insult to injury, she was stripped of every emotion she had left, which she could only recover while drunk, essentially making her an empty husk whose void only could be filled by consuming the very thing that emptied her in the first place. 8:57 AM ---- With Elthara’s usefulness having reached its end, the devil she worked for abandoned her, and suddenly she found herself alone in a dangerous world that would kill her sooner or later if she didn’t cooperate with other people. At the beginning, Elthara had a rough time connecting with other people, yet as time passed and after she joined a novice adventurer party that accepted her, she slowly started to reconnect with those “weakening” emotions she once had lost, and nowadays she’s trying to atone for all the harm she had done despite knowing that won’t undo anything. One day, after celebrating with her partners another successful adventure, Elthara felt a bit dizzy after her seventh drink and wanted to go outside to get some air, yet when she crossed the door, her consciousness faded away, and when she woke up, she found herself in Ao. Tink. Tink. "The stars looks so beautiful", Atlas thought. Tink. Tink. Tink. He laid facing towards the sky, the cold yet refreshing water rhythmically battering against his armor. Some of which slipped their way past his defenses onto his face. From his mouth a line of blood dribbled and stained the inside of his suit. This was it, his final moments. A barricades spear had pierced between his metal plate and into him. His hands instinctually gripped his weapon, slowly slipping as his body relaxed. The faint clashing of metal, magic, and rush of feet on mud filled the air around him. Dreams, friends, hope- all of it halted, meaningless in this moment. He wanted to do more. He regretted he couldn't press forward. "Is it my time to see Pharasma?" he thought, closing his eyes one final time. Until nothing. Suddenly, he felt his spirit, body, and mind all align for just a moment. Wild colors and images flashed before him. His mind raced, overwhelmed with information. Then nothing. Grass. Dirt. Headache. He awoke after a period, looking around. His wounds were healed, and he was in unfamiliar territory. He had arrived in Ao. 1:24 PM This is but a brief telling of Atlas' life - and death. Many other lessons shaped who he is today, some of which include romance, discipline, betrayal, mischief, heartbreak, and many more. Atlas had a relatively simple upbringing. A loving family, a few siblings, inspiration to look forward to. His father was an alchemist, and mother a herbalist. Both of which worked together in a beautiful unison as the tribe's medicinal aid and doctors. The tribe itself was nomadic. There were a few events that shaped Atlas' life. The first one was their time near the Five Kings Mountains, getting involved in Dwarven culture. Everything from their expert craft, their pantheons and beliefs, and even their language. In particular he enjoyed hearing about Pharasma, the other world, and spirits. The cycle of life, now enlightened with the cycle of death. The second was near The River Kingdoms, where his tribe had been attacked by marauders. There he learned protection, throwing himself in front of some of his younger siblings and standing strong. Of course, fending them off the best he could until the real cavalry of the tribe was able to save him. From that point, he trained with the others to become a warrior. He showed proficiency and passion in defending others, and he seemed to know his way around armor. Perhaps this was because of his interest he showed with the dwarves and their mighty mobile metal walls. 1:24 PM The final is a series of events. First, Godsrain. The death of the war God Gorum devastated the entire world of Golarion. His tribe fractured, some seemingly hopeless. Others driven by greed to seek divinity or wealth. His family wasn't spared, and many of his siblings reached to a darker side of themselves. His parents had to establish themselves and continue using their skills in a settlement in a hope to survive. Atlas did everything he could to help them and try to persuade his people, rallying them. Seeing as Atlas isn't the most charismatic person, this wasn't very successful. The world had been drawn into chaos. A middling alchemist himself, barely even able to provide help to his father, had to seek independence. What else was he better at than protecting people? He found himself hired as a sort of adventurer in Sandpoint. The Tuatha De Dannan weren’t the first people to invade this paradise, but it was their will that they would be the shepherds of the land, and ensure that the land wasn’t exploited and destroyed. Love made them decide to keep the land. Fear made them take action to defend it. The Fir Bolg were all but indigenous to the land, but their resistance had been brief, tempered when they saw that the Tuatha De were able to build and grow in harmony with the land. It was the Fomorians that made the Tuatha De begin to take drastic measures, towering brutes who took advantage of all kindness, and saw everything as theirs. An architect who was known for pulling the very metal for her spires from ore without disturbing stone, Brigh, was tasked to forge an undying force against the titanic Fomorians. Muin does not remember much of her life from before she was tasked to take on her metallic shell. She remembered being a slight, weak chinned, cowardly man, focused more on clock making and drawing than defending Eiru. She had been a student under Brigh, not the best or the brightest, but far from the worst of her apprentices. Her skill with working with machines had made her a clear candidate to aid the war effort as a mechanic, but her weak body was the issue, should she see combat. She doesn’t remember if she resisted or resented, but based on her later path, she reasons that she likely was happy to get out of that miserable pile of secrets, and become someone admirable. She had joined Brigh’s weapon against the Fomorians, a group of living weapons able to fight and die alongside their Shide brethren, only to be rebuilt so long as their nigh indestructible core could be recovered. The Mechanical Shide Unbroken, MSU, Muin Sil Ur phonetically, were among the many weapons brought to bear against the raiding giants, and helped to rebuff them from the paradise. 6:55 PM Their names were taken from them as a way to ease the passing, along with many of their personal memories. All that was supposed to remain was their skill and their compassion for their fellows. Not a person. Just a number, and a mission. Eventually, the Fomorians were defeated, and peace subsequently settled into Eiru. All of the MSU units were put into storage, set aside, should the land need to go to war again. But the Tuatha De Dannin were innovators, and built contingency upon contingency. By the time the Milasian Humans invaded, they were buried under centuries of other plans B through R, and were left untouched by the time the Humans were victorious, and the land was split between the Tuatha De and the Milasians, with the humans on the Material, and the Shide in the First World. For centuries, row upon row of automatons stood at attention, the kelly green of their lights softly breathing in standby. And then, for no known reason at all, the light in Muin blinked white, and then blue. She tried to stay in attention, her light wavering as she hummed along to an old song in the back of her mind, looking over the blank canvases that were her former compatriots. She tried counting schematics. She tried tensing and releasing her motivators. For whatever reason, she could never go into standby for longer than a couple hours. After a decade conscious, she finally gave up, and decided to busy her hands. She started with the MSU’s nearest her, engraving designs and patterns. One she made camo, another she made look like they were dressed in a smart suit. By the time she tattooed a few score of them, she felt confident doing the same on herself. She was surprised to feel that the engraving process actually hurt, but eventually she had covered herself in pink and white engravings, to compliment her glowing blue core and compressors. 6:57 PM After nigh a century of busing herself, she decided to move on. No one was coming for them. She couldn't wake the other MSU’s. She had to find something that stimulated her mind. Taking only her tools and her weapons, she burrowed her way out of the hold. But the world she found was far different from what she could have imagined. The people were alien to her, some calling her demon, others curious about her strange look and armaments. After a time of touring what these lands had turned to, Muin settled into a quiet existence, learning the Milasian culture, the intricacies of their machines, and even how to engrave the people's skins. The occasional call to help with some invading monster or the other kept her weeks lively, and using her rudimentary magics to help those around that her skills couldn't was always nice. One day, Muin opened the door of her workshop to find different morning stars above, and different buildings surrounding her humble workshop. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Woods | Hjalmar 3 | Aetyrin 3 5/8/2026 11:31 PM Name: Aetyrin Wildstrider Ancestry: Elf Heritage: Custom Mixed Heritage - Human Class: Spellshot Gunslinger | Storm Druid Age: 53 Backstory: Aetyrin Wildwalker had it all. He had Everspring, a bountiful home amidst emerald groves and roaring rivers, close companionship amidst his druid circle, and a sense of purpose. Nights were often spent wandering beneath the stars or sharing drinks around a fire, and his fellow acolytes of the Green Faith were his confidants. As a Warden, it was Aetyrin’s job to seek out and eliminate threats that encroached upon his circle’s lands, preferably with as little disruption to Everspring and its surrounding forests as possible. In the weeks leading up to his own convergence, Aetyrin had begun to notice an uptick of Outsiders streaming through his home. Demons, fey, devils and more were roaming in greater numbers than he and his fellow Wardens could handle. Not understanding the cause, and fearful that these invaders (the demons in particular) would destroy their beautiful home, Aetyrin and his Wardens withdrew further and further into the heart of their grove. It was time to observe, study, and prepare. Aetyrin threw himself into learning everything that he could, seeking weaknesses to exploit, patterns to understand, and forces to redirect. It was one late night, while studying in the library, that the Abyss broke loose upon the grove. Demons poured in, slaughtering and burning everything they could get their tainted claws on. Aetyrin saw his entire life’s work torn apart and put to the torch in front of him, as he fought in vain to stem the demonic tide. When the massive oak at the heart of Everspring was cast down and the spring was poisoned, he knew he had lost. Aetyrin fled the ruins of his home, hoping to at least find survivors and make their way to less hostile lands to seek shelter. 11:31 PM During his search through the wilderness, Aetyrin stepped through the gap between two entwined trees that were blocking his path. On the other side of that gap, he found himself in a land completely unfamiliar. He was standing in a doorway, in a city, on a mountaintop, in an entirely different plane. His attempts to return home by stepping back through the doorway proved fruitless. He had been called to the Hall of Arrival, like many before him. With nowhere else to turn, and no home to return to even if he did find a way back, Aetyrin pressed on. Luckily, Axiom is a city flush with knowledge and full of fellow adventurers also seeking new ground under their feet. Aetyrin, Wayfinder in hand, began to wander once again, exploring the bizarre new world of Ao, always on the lookout for demons, undead and other ilk, with two words circling in the back of his mind: “Never again.” 11:31 PM Kobold! 11:35 PM Character has been set up in Foundry! I did have a question: would it be possible to use either dual Rotary Bows or a Taw Launcher (with Unconventional Weaponry)? Their item descriptions list them as crossbows, but it looks like Paizo missed updating those two (as well as the Repeating Crossbow and Crescent Cross) to the new Crossbow weapon group when they remastered the Treasure Vault book. So, RAW, they don't get Gunslinger proficiency. But it seems like RAI that they should since the book calls them crossbows and the art is of a crossbow. 11:36 PM It'd be doable by manually swapping the Group for the item on Foundry, but it's obviously up to the council of GMs on if they'd be ok with that. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Urquhart|Goresh 3|Helm 2 5/9/2026 2:35 PM Name: Goresh Ancestry: Automaton Heritage: Droomar Class: Beast Summoner | Paradox Witch Age: Old enough to have seen the stars wander and the great trees grow Backstory For centuries, Goresh wandered the world without purpose and without a name. His original one had been forgotten long ago. His metal frame, once bright and strong, had rusted under endless seasons of wind and snow. When he reached the frozen lands of the Mammoth Lords, he collapsed among the tundra stones. A tribe of orcs found him there—followers of Skode, who saw in his endurance the mark of divine strength. They carried him back to their camp, repaired his broken joints with bone and hide, and wrapped him in mammoth furs. He became known as Goresh—a guardian of the tribe and a symbol of endurance. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Helena|Bramble 6|Nué 4|Siv 2 5/17/2026 1:29 PM Name: Siv Ulriksdóttir Ancestry: Kitsune Heritage: Frozen Wind Kitsune Class: Oscillating Wave Psychic (Gathered Lore) | Outwit Ranger Age: 24 Backstory Siv Ulriksdóttir's tailless form has a tail. As a kitsune, this makes her somewhat of an oddity. But there's a perfectly reasonable explanation for this. It just needs a bit of context. So let us begin at the beginning. Long ago, a group of frozen wind kitsune endeavored to chart an expedition across the Crown of the World itself, hiking from Tian Xia all the way to Avistan, loosely along the Path of Aganhei. To their surprise, they handily succeeded, for the most part. They did, however, stray a bit too far from the path in the Rimethirst Mountains, and were hunted by giants no longer contract-bound to leave them be. This deviation from their route led them to a settlement they did not know existed, a community of fiendish nephilim well-suited to the chill of the peaks, who hid them away and sheltered them from the giants. These nephilim were all runaways for various reasons - persecution in Cheliax, forced conscription in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, and an infestation of demons in Sarkoris numbering among them. The kitsune knew what it was like living secretively away from a world that wouldn't care to understand their way of life. So it was the two communities bonded, and after publishing an account of most of their journey down the Path of Aganhei, omitting information about the nephilim of course, the kitsune decided to return and live alongside the nephilim, joining their two families and using their innate magic to help support their way of life. Atop the nearby mountain, they built a shrine in thanks to their gods Daikitsu and Yamatsumi. (1/?, there's more coming shortly) ----------------- Character is uploaded and ready to review on the Foundry Server thank you @Sheet Checker s! 1:30 PM It was into this community that Siv was born, and given a name in honor of the leader of the Thanelandic nephilim that saved her people, Ulrik. As many kitsune tend to mimic the type of folk they grow up around with their tailless form, it felt natural for her to take on the appearance of a nephilim to better fit in with friends and family. She came to be proud of the form, as it represented people she looked up to and cherished. In fact, Siv felt and still feels more comfortable in her tailless form than in her native kitsune fur, identifying more with it than the foxlike appearance of her blood relatives. She valued her people's culture and traditions as much as the nephilims’, this was simply what felt right. In spite of the harsh and unforgiving environment she grew up in, Siv had a happy childhood, with plenty of time to find herself and discover her passions. And there was nothing Siv was more passionate about than monsters. From the moment Siv caught her first glimpse of a yeti, she fell in love with the idea of finding out everything about it. What it ate, how it hunted, where it lived, how it raised children… she needed to decipher the mystery of this new creature. And when she found out there were more strange monsters around her home, she had to know about them too. This thirst for knowledge quickly took on a different bent when she realized what she knew could help her people hunt the creatures around their home and secure food and livelihood for their community. She practiced every day with the bow, and studied by candlelight into the night, learning which vital spots to hit for a quick, clean kill without spoiling the meat. And she was good at it. Siv's knowledge made her useful to her village, and she found she loved feeling useful. She named her young drake Skald after both the language and the poets, as he always had a bit of a contemplative look about him, like a scaly poet pondering his next verse. She loves him with all her heart, and to her, he's as much family as any beloved pet can be. When raising Skald, Siv started to feel a sort of connection to the inner fire of her companion, feeling kinship to him as she had the same flame in her own heart, steady growing. She found that the combination of her inner fire and her connection to the cold from the environment she'd been raised in and her bloodline allowed her to manipulate a sort of balance, using the strength of her will to bend flame and frost to her whims. Lurking in every shadow Staring right at you? She walks She is coming… … closer. 12:47 PM Now I commit this record to ink and parchment. For if I perish before I find my way back to my origin, my story, written by fate and played by me, will be remembered. Through it's will perhaps these words will make it back to my people. This is the tale of The Dark Empress. I was born under the embrace of the night sky in a small crux just north of Aelyosos. Being surrounded by the myth and legend of the land brought us closer to fate, and thus gave our settlement much more permanence than other cruxes. My guardians spoke much of the hero-gods of old and the cyclopean mysticism that gave them their pusedo-divinity. “This, too, was the will of fate” explained my father, who always took on the mask of a gravely old sage when teaching me history. Fate cast the Cyclops in the role of tragic enlightened seers–giving them an iota of it’s power to make their predictions, but dooming them to fall into darkness. A dramatic end. Naturally, after growing out of the phase of wanting to become a cyclops, I sought to understand every single facet of Fate. Starting with the ancient techniques of myth-speaking. This, too, was the will of fate. A century it took for my story to truly begin. In which Nocturne and I, my partner in everything, scoured the lands of Iblydos for all their secrets. The sins of the Ghol-Gan, the exact prophecies of hero-gods old and ancient–which always took the form of a story. When my knowledge proved sufficient I left the archipelago for my next task: The Harrow, and thus the Varisian people. Far north-west did I travel, taking on a mortal guise of a hooded masked figure cloaked head to toe, a course set for the lands of Ustalav. It was then, I met her. 12:48 PM She had many names. Beauty incarnate, a wisp of the sun, fate’s gift to me. A simple woman in all honesty. She came to me at sunset while I posed as a street fortune-teller to unravel the secrets of The Harrow, all anxiety trapped behind scarlet eyes and fair skin. A divination she sought to reveal the fate behind an upcoming excursion, for she was a adventurer of little repute. Yes. The moment I laid eyes I knew she would be my muse, my hero-god. A crimson blaze for all of the world to witness. This, too, was the will of fate. She perished not more than a month after our first meeting. Her party overrun by the forces of evil, but they live now because she gave her life for theirs. I laid eyes upon her and she breathed her last. Surrounded by carnage and viscera. She could not have possibly recognized me without my guise, atop my steed cloaked in shadow, headless, but she smiled anyway when she saw me. She spoke highly of heroics and she got her wish. I cannot see the appeal. I thought I had grew complacent. Trying to play god-maker. So I threw myself into my work as a proper sibyl for my peers. Going from crux to crux teaching all that I had learned, while fulfilling my role as a proper Dullahan. Excising any who would disrupt fate, or escape their destiny. I cloaked my heart in shadows, finally becoming The Dark Empress. My mentors. They worried for my heart, that I had become the mask. They urged me to face whatever darkness clung to me, lest I forget myself and become a wretch. I knew they were right. After twenty-eight years I returned to her. It was pouring that night, with devastating winds. So much so that it seemed like the gods were weeping for her. It was easy to find her grave amongst the others–a blade shattered at the fuller lay on the soil facing her headstone. Rust beginning to eat at it. I dismounted Nocturne and approached. The moment my finger touched her head stone the world swam with color. Earth cracked under her grave and split apart, sending Nocturne and I falling towards the infinite. I lost consciousness for and inordinate amount of time, but I dreamed. I never dreamed before, but I dreamed of her. When I woke my surroundings were different. Everything felt strange. Then I heard her voice and looked down. Parthenas was in my lap, her scarlet eyes boring into where I assume my face would be if I had one. I could hear her voice again. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Krutoy | Damian2 6/21/2026 5:37 PM Name: Damian Rottguard Ancestry: Human Heritage: Skilled Human (Society) Class: Flurry Ranger | Mastermind Rogue Age: 21 Backstory: Damian Rottguard was born in Golarion in the city of Opparos to a noble family, the Rottguards. They were a minor house in the city, but a fairly wealthy one. They owned a large wine vineyard and production facility, and they made good money from it. Damian was the first born of the Rottguards, so he was the shining son of his family. His father, Augustus Rottguard spared no expense with his son’s education. Damian received the best tutors and swordmasters, and he took well to the teaching. Well, anyone would take well to it with the money Augustus was spending on tutorage. Of all the teachings Damian took to, he enjoyed his sword training the most, and, as he grew older, he started in the dueling circuit at Opparos, doing very well there. Occasionally, he would visit other towns to establish wine trades, but, in truth, it was mostly to duel other people and learn other sword arts. Eventually, people stopped dueling him. The other nobility would purposefully avoid dueling him in the circuits due to the risk of losing. Few nobility were as obsessed as Damian with their training. Damian grew frustrated with dueling the same opponents and took matters into his own hands. He became somewhat of a scoundrel. He would insult or coerce the other nobility into dueling him. These would progress into greater insults and more bolder accusations from him as he goaded more people into duels. However, all of this came to a head when, at a masquerade ball, he became romantically involved with the betrothed of another guests. She was the betrothed of Octavius Stavian, one of the sons of the royal family. But, instead of being goaded into a duel, Octavius took a different approach. Octavius hired The Golden Hand, a band of ruthless mercenaries, to take out Damian. A few weeks after the ball, they besieged the Rottguard estate. But Damian was not there. He was out on the town drinking and carousing. He only arrived home the next morning, still drunk, to a smoldering ruin. He was devastated, his world gone, and, while his family faced this, he was out carousing. He was not stupid, he knew Octavius was behind this, for he still hadn't accepted Damian's duel, but Damian was reckless. Name: Fidget Ancestry: Gnome Heritage: Otter Beastkin Class: Inventor/Champion Age: 24 Backstory: Fidget the otter-person was found near a small, nondescript village in the middle of nowhere. There were no signs of her parents or other family. She was taken in by the town librarian since most of this town wanted nothing to do with this random beast child. The librarian had a daughter of about the same age. The girl was frail and sickly and would often be bedridden until she lost the ability to walk altogether. This was somewhat offset by her psychic abilities. Fidget would be the one to craft the girl's wheelchair, although not without being told to not add in a bunch of "innovations." Fidget, having grown up in a library, loved to read. Her favorite stories were about heroes. Selfless champions who would do anything to protect others, no matter the personal cost. Her favorite story was about Acavna, the hero who sacrificed herself to move the moon in the path of a falling meteor, saving the entire planet from destruction at the cost of her life. Fidget had vowed to be the girl's hero, and soon, she would have the chance to become a full-fledged hero in her own right. 7:29 PM One day, the small town was besieged by the undead. Fidget, the girl, and a few others defended the village and fought off the undead. But soon after, people all over town started getting sick, a plague had begun spreading. Fidget and the girl left the town in search of help and a cure. Along the way, they found a strange building. Inside were scientific wonders Fidget could only have dreamed about. Computers and machines, flying robotic drones that shot lasers at the group and other such marvels. Fidget and her friends smashed the drones and then... They exploded. Fidget remembers pushing the girl's wheelchair away to save her, but got caught in the blast. She accepted this fate, knowing that she had at least saved the girl's life. 7:30 PM Fidget was... Somewhere else. She knew nothing of this town but had no choice but to begin life anew there, alone. She set up a lab in the nearby forest where she got to work trying to create technology like she'd seen in that building. She was obsessed and eventually she created her power armor. Her joy was short lived as soon after, her new home was once again set upon by the undead. Fidget fought off the undead, but, of course, the plague had begun spreading through her new home again. Fidget had no choice but to go find people who could help her. Once again, she never made it to a cure. While traveling, she heard the girl's voice in her head. The girl who had become a distant memory... Fidget had even forgotten her name... A psychic rift, a loved one trying desperately to bring her back... But once again, Fidget found herself in a mysterious place, meeting a mysterious.... Person? At least she thinks it was a person? It merely pointed and Fidget found a place once again technologically fascinating beyond anything she had seen. And this is where Fidget's newest journey would begin, on Ao, in Axiom. She knows this time she can succeed and become a true hero! 7:30 PM Kobold! TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Lynn - Lirrel 2/Tesna 2 6/24/2026 1:58 AM Name: Tesna Ancestry: Minotaur Heritage: Dwarf Class: Inventor | Fighter Age: 28 Backstory The brisk town of Snowford, in the foothills of the Mindspin Mountains, was the place young Tesna called home. Living with her mother, she was a foolhardy, inquisitive sort, always fascinated with the workings of things, utterly convinced that she could make improvements. Others insisted his father's bloodline carried an ancient curse. Fear and superstition soon turned to open distrust. Unwilling to risk what the clan might do if those suspicions continued to grow, Adius's parents left the nomadic herd and settled in The Eldergreens, one of the few permanent centaur farming settlements that cared for the elderly, the disabled, and those unable to follow the endless migrations. Adius grew up working the fields and helping care for those who called the Eldergreens home. In the evenings, retired adventurers and old warriors would tell stories of brave knights and wandering heroes who slew monsters, defended the innocent, and stood against impossible odds. Adius hung on every word. Before long, he knew exactly what he wanted to become. While he was still young, those ideals were put to the test. Raiders descended upon the quiet community, cutting down those too old to defend themselves. When Adius saw one of the raiders bearing down on his friends and family, he charged with nothing but determination. As he sprang through the fields, a crimson spear suddenly manifested in his hands. He had no idea what it was or why it answered his call, only that it had appeared when others needed him most. Guided by instinct, he drove the spear through the raider and fought alongside his neighbors until the invaders were driven away. The battle was won, but at a terrible cost. Among the dead were several of the elderly adventurers whose stories had inspired Adius since he was a foal. The stories he had grown up hearing were no longer distant legends—they were proof that the world desperately needed people willing to stand between the innocent and danger, and Adius devoted himself to becoming one of those heroes. When he came of age, Adius sought out knightly orders, only to find every door closed to him. Some claimed he was too old to begin as a squire. Others insisted a centaur was simply too large to train. Many rejected him outright because of the crimson skin, horns, and devil's tail that marked his fiendish heritage. Refusing to abandon his dream, Adius found another path. He hired himself out to caravan guards, mercenary companies, and retired soldiers, trading hard work and coin for whatever lessons they were willing to teach. His ability to manifest a crimson spear was rare, and many of his employers took pride in having such an unusual warrior in their service. Over years of wandering, escorting caravans, and countless hours of practice, Adius slowly forged himself into the warrior he had always aspired to become. Eventually, Adius struck out on his own. He earned an honest living guarding caravans, hunting brigands, and traveling from village to village, where he trained local militias and aspiring youths to better defend themselves. Though some were wary of his fiendish appearance, those who fought and traveled beside him quickly learned that his word was good and his resolve unwavering. Before long, he built a quiet reputation as someone who could always be counted on to answer a call for help. Though he never performed the grand deeds celebrated in songs or earned the title of knight, it was a humble but meaningful life. Even so, there were quiet moments when Adius found himself wondering if he had fallen short of the dream that had first taken root in the fields of the Eldergreens. While escorting a merchant caravan, Adius spotted a wagon careening uncontrollably down a steep hill. A child stood frozen in its path. Without hesitation, he charged. He reached the child just in time, throwing them clear of the wagon's path. There was no time left to save himself. The impact came, and everything went dark. 7:28 PM When Adius opened his eyes again, he found himself in another world: Ao. Not every Demon is made from a lost soul, and not every soul that ends up in the Outer Rifts is there because they were judged. Sometimes someone makes a very stupid and painful mistake. If the fate are especially cruel someone like Abfell gets to exist. He never met his parents. All he knows is that one was an Elf and the other a Demon, and that they died or sold him soon after his birth. The half demon spent millennium being traded from one master to another. From the putrid swamp of Mephizim , to the burning sands of Kuthan , And even the broken streets of Ghahazi he learned everything the Rifts could teach him about fear, pain and domination. So it went for uncounted years until he was traded to an ambitious greater demon. A nalfeshnee looking to make a splash on the mortal world. Seeing his chance Abfell did everything he could to be in the right place at the right time in order to come with his master on a trip to Golaron. Once there he laid his trap. Taking weeks to plant the right words and leave the right evidence to convince his masters mortal allies that the fat pig was going to betray them far sooner then was expected. While his master and the humans were killing each other Abfell pretended to fight on his masters side; letting him wear himself out. When the last human was dead the nalfeshnee was on his last legs. This was his moment . Tackling the fat pig to the ground Abfell preformed a ritual he had learned in the slave pens. One for transferring the slave bond from one slave to another. However he had altered it. He traded his spiritual bonds for his masters boundless Need, his unending drive for More. As the Pig was dragged kicking and squealing back to a new life of slavery in the rifts Abfell decided to fill the new void in his soul with the one thing he always wanted; Freedom. The idyllic fishing village was quiet, serene, and beyond the birth of a new child or the union between two families, uneventful. It was no small wonder that the young Barakos was restless. Countless nights, the boy would sit under the stars and dream of adventure. The opportunity arrived in the form of a mysterious isle visible from the shores that appeared suddenly one night. On the isle was a gigantic door, holding what seemed to be a dangerous dungeon. The villagers of Duskview feared what may arrive if this door were to spring open, and made an open plea to adventurers who were willing to delve into its depths. Waves of adventurers came to plunder the dungeon, few returned unharmed, but those who did came back with gold and valuables. Soon, Duskview became flooded with people seeking treasure and those catered to buying and selling to said adventurers. Barakos knew he could not miss his chance but with no experience and no equipment, he was swiftly rejected by any organized party. It wasn’t until Barakos met Iskandor that things changed. The veteran dwarf recognized Barakos’ physical strength and size as an asset and hired him as a pack mule. Despite his otherwise menial job, Barakos happily accepted his role. The party’s initial success led them and others to travel deeper and deeper into the dungeon. But many soon found that their well traveled paths had shifted and they could not escape. Panic set in among many groups as adventurers turned against one another for supplies and monsters became more aggressive and dangerous. Steadily, the other members of Barakos’ party lost their lives. (edited) 11:26 AM Barakos survived, alone, fending for himself against seasoned warriors and vicious creatures, surviving off of fresh water fountains that seemed to appear randomly throughout the dungeon and the flesh of “appropriate” monsters. Unbeknownst to the doomed adventurers, the whole structure was an experiment of the god Lamashtu. Monsters of all kinds were concentrated into one space until the most dangerous of all is left, the process creating a creature with the most advantageous traits. Lamashtu’s experiment yielded great fruit. The surviving creatures, Barakos among them, began to mutate adopting abilities and physical traits from creatures they conquered. The dungeon’s distorted sense of time and lack of a visible sun made it difficult for Barakos to identify how long he had been trapped in its depths but his time was suddenly cut short when the whole structure began to shift suddenly, as if tumbling through the air. Once it stopped, Barakos noticed that the paths and doorways throughout the dungeon remained consistent and finally, he was able to find the door and leave. When finally, he was able to see the land outside of the dungeon, he found himself looking not at Duskview but at the new world of Ao. With nothing left to go back to and his experience fresh in his mind, Barakos began to travel the world, helping people in hunting down dangerous monsters and other beasts. The current ruler of Saltspire Thalassar Corallis was a young dragon when his family was brought to Ao and has done much to reform his families empire on this new world. His daughters Vyrissel and Azura Corallis are his heirs and the ones who he hopes to one day take over his control of the kingdom. The Selection House Corallis keeps a large and varied menagerie of aquatic creatures within Saltspire. This is due to a custom passed down where young royalty will select a group of these creatures as pets. This acts as a means to accustom them to looking after not one but many. Among this menagerie one of the oldest and unassuming groups were the trilobites. One of few creatures that managed to follow house Corallis to Ao. Due to their proximity with the dragons and the convergence they had somewhat awoken sentience. It was due to this spark of intelligence that Vyrissel Corallis selected them when the time came. Though they were odd creatures Vyrissel was happy with her decision and took care of them like any other. As time went on both Vyrissel and the colony grew in body, mind, and power. An Error As Vyrissel raised the colony she came to realize that they were more than they seemed. Unlike other creatures they absorbed magic like a battery. Invested in their growth she would feed them magic through various spells as she learned them. Eventually through a sort of sign language they were able to communicate. Around this time Vyrissel had been taught the secret technique of House Corallis which allowed them to take humanoid forms. Not realizing the implications she decided to pass it on to the colony who learned it quickly like any other spell. Now able to take a human form and given the name of Mia they became friends. The Ancient Laws Something that Vyrissel had forgotten due to her young age was that the rites of transfiguration she had learned were not to be taught to those without the name Corallis. Vyrissel could pass on the name Corallis to Mia in a way similar to selecting a knight, but Vyrissel would become responsible for Mia's actions and if Vyrissel's status were in question Mia could lose hers. With no real option they were both quick to accept the offer and soon after Mia was taken out of Saltspire's territory. 2:58 PM The Exile Now alone Mia found theirself aimlessly drifting for some time. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Ggator|Viola8|Simon12|Bargu12 3/23/2026 7:25 PM Spoilers for ATSS (Ashes that Still Stir) Name: Viola Decker Ancestry: Human Heritage: Oread Class: Gunslinger (Drifter) | Monk Age: 61 Backstory Viola Decker lived and died in the desert of New Osirion. In her entire life she never strayed outside the desert for she was always tied down. Her father was a ruthless outlaw by the name of Jeb Decker and she never knew her mother. Jeb however was the leader of the Dead Deck gang. A notorious gang of outlaws that were detestable human beings. Viola was always sickened by how they acted but was unable to leave. She shut out that side of her life through the art of gunplay. Her father would just think that it was her following in his footsteps after all. Time passed and Viola put up the facade of a ruthless killer. She would secretly allow those she was tasked with killing escape outside of the desert. As many outlaws do her father met an early grave. Viola became the obvious replacement as leader of the gang. Now holding the power Viola attempted to find a way out, but she was not quick enough. She had a child, a little girl, who she did not wish to grow up in the same environment she did. The other outlaws in the gang saw her weakness and capitalized on it. The pressed a young outlaw named Luther Good into kidnapping her daughter. He failed but she would not let it slide. Unaware of her own gangs involvement she challenged Luther to a duel. It was the last thing she needed to do before she could close this chapter of her life for good. That never happened though. On her way to duel Luther the train Viola was sabotaged and plummeted into a canyon killing everyone onboard. That canyon became a mass grave and for 20 years set idle, but one day the resentful soul of Viola rose once more. She had only one thing on her mind and that was finishing where she left off by killing Luther Good. Before she could though a group of mercenaries snuffed out her second chance. A few weeks later she returned but now in a much worse state. Coming back the first time was easy but the second expended much more energy. She sat in that canyon now much calmer. It was at this point that she realized that she was likely set up. She gathered herself and set out into the desert. Her new target was the old members of the Dead Deck Gang that had conspired to kill her and threatened the life of her daughter. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Col. | Skarn 4 3/26/2026 1:18 PM Name: Skarn "The Thunderhead" Ancestry: Titan Heritage: Energy Spark Class: Giant Instinct Barbarian | Exemplar Age: 3000 Backstory Skarn "The Thunderhead" was not born a towering demigod, but as a surprisingly heavy infant to two ordinary human parents in the storm-swept valleys of an ancient fantasy realm. For his first decade, he was simply the largest, strongest boy in the village, but as he entered his teenage years, a dormant, primordial bloodline violently awakened. He didn't just hit a growth spurt; he erupted into a 12-foot-tall Titan. His mortal flesh became etched with glowing blue runes, and wings of pure, crackling electricity sprouted from his back. Despite the terrifying manifestation of his true nature, his parents' love never wavered, and Skarn swore to be the immovable sentinel of their valley. Over the next three millennia, Skarn outlived his mortal family by epochs, wielding a colossal greataxe forged from fallen thunderbolts to protect the countless generations of his village's descendants from empires and monstrous threats alike. Skarn’s 3,000-year vigil was finally shattered not by an invading army, but by a catastrophic Convergence Event that tore the very fabric of his reality apart. The sky above his ancestral valley fractured, screaming with chaotic, unnatural planar energies that even his immense strength could not hold back. He planted his massive, heavily armored feet and raised his axe to intercept the rift's destructive magic, attempting to shield the descendants he had sworn to protect. Instead, the anomaly swallowed him whole—along with the very earth he stood on—and violently slammed them into the plane of Ao. Now stranded near the city of Axiom, the ancient juggernaut finds himself a guardian without his original world. Still crackling with the displaced fury of his lost realm, Skarn navigates this strange new reality, ready to unleash his primordial storms to protect the fragile lives of those newly caught in the Convergence. ----------------- Character is uploaded and ready to review on the Foundry Server thank you @Sheet Checker s! While not xenophobic, the feline tribes of the isles had reason to keep themselves secretive from their neighbours, as dictated to them by the demigod-like being called Twin Moons Jaguar who was both their tribe's progenitor and its guardian. Blessed by the Moon with a form of both man and beast he passed these traits along to his descendants, populating the tribe along with his mate, Sovereign Heart of the Rapturous Liberty, his Sun-blessed soul-twin, and thus the Tribes of Cinder rose to prominence and spread across the archipelago of islands that were their home. Jaguar and Sovereign were beings of celestial descent hunted by the largest nation of the plane upon which they dwelt - an empire who saw it as their divine mission to exterminate all who bore the 'taint' of celestial interference as they saw it. For a time, the twin demigods were able to escape the ire of their would-be executioners by lying low, using their powers only for the benefit of their children and beloved people rather than answering to the higher calling of heroism that boiled in their veins, for as exemplars of the Sun and Moon as they were they were expected to do great things, were it not for a great curse laid upon their kind in aeons past. Throughout their endeavours Weloh-Ir mostly hid in the back, hiding in the shadows of whoever was farthest from the adversaries. Over time, as Weloh-Ir got older the group started to teach them a variety of useful skills, but given their propensity to hide, Saevel decided against teaching them close quarters combat and instead taught them to strengthen their body. Then when Weloh-Ir turned 18, Rergif and Ariwyn described what happened all those years ago, that brought them to their group. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter 8Plat: Baiwak9 Tarachi6 Della2 4/2/2026 7:45 AM Name: Della Talmon Ancestry: Halfling Aiuvarin Heritage: Jaric Halfling through mother, Vourinoi Elf through father. Class: Justice Champion of Arazni | Wit Swashbuckler Age: 28 Appearance: Tall for a halfling at almost four feet, Della is a lean and harsh looking member of her ancestry. With a sharp aquiline nose, hooded dark eyes, and skin the color of ashen sandstone. Her ears are long for a halfling as well, betraying her Aiuvarin status. She dresses in drab Jaric robes of pale purples and reds, faded to almost grey, with a brilliant crimson bladed scarf wrapped over her head, giving her a modest hijab to allow her to blend into crowds when she needs, or a long flowing cape when she wants to show off. She is armored with sparse leather plates protecting her dueling arm, with hidden plates under her bodice and skirt to add to her duplicity. On her hip lies a long rapier sheath, with the basket of a modest blade held within, but when she draws her blade, the flowing shifting blood of her sword may be any weapon she needs. Underneath her hijab, her dark curly hair is trimmed into a short mop of a hyena mohawk, bearing her grudge with her at all times. 7:45 AM Backstory: Born to a hard working Jaric Halfling woman and a forlorn Vourinoi Elf in the barrier mountains of western Katapesh, Della had a hard childhood. Soon after her fourth name day, her father left to seek greener pastures, and her mother was forced to sell their modest farm and move to Solku to live in the slums. To make ends meet, both women worked at a local farm, harvesting crops for coppers a day. One day while they were in the fields working, the farm where they worked was beset by Kholo bandits, taking Della to be sold as chattel in the slave markets of Katapesh City. Small hands work well in mills, and halfling children were sold at a premium to them en masse, and Della’s swift hands were adroit at keeping massive looms untangled and climbing deftly through the machines. But children only stay young for so long, and her owners saw her as an asset to be sold to those who have a more base need for her form. Sold she was to a seedy pesh den, with seedier clientele who were used to having their way with the attendants. She resisted as long as she could. But the clients were strong, rutting beasts, the pesh hot in their veins, and her resistance was only a challenge to be bested. They plied her with the drug to quiet her screams. And tolerance only diminishes, and eventually addiction forms. She would like to claim she never cried. One night, when a particularly brutal client was done with her, one of the older attendants tended to her broken and bruised body, and told her the story of the Queen of Geb, Arazni. How she was once a proud and respected name in the Inner Sea, but by the machinations of cruel men, she was now seen as a plaything to suit the appetites of others. How one day she would transcend, no longer the ‘Whore Queen,” and she would have her cruel, cold, justice. 7:46 AM . The story sat with Della for years, keeping a glimmer of faith in her eyes, even as the narcotic glazed them over. She tried many times to surrender, to give up, and return to peace the only way she knew how, but self-inflicted wounds are as easy to tend to as those administered by the clients. They always brought her back, only to be put back to work when her wounds were healed. Things changed one day, while entertaining a group of Okeno pirates, when Della was particularly disgusted by their actions. Maybe the pesh wasn’t hitting right. Maybe she’d just had enough. But she does clearly remember a single word, a voice not her own, feminine and stern, searing into her mind; ”Resist.” The ensuing brawl resulted in the pesh den being burned down, taking a large section of a bazaar with it. Running from hiding spot to hiding spot, gripping the shattered half of a pirate's rapier to her chest, she managed to avoid the gaze of the patrolling aluums and zephyr guards. But her freedom was short-lived. She may have escaped bondage, but chains within her veins were far stronger, and pesh was surprisingly hard to come by. One day, while shaking down a pesh vendor in the city to get her fix, a group of Firebrands found her, seeking to interrogate the same man for another purpose. They saw that she was destined for a greater purpose than the fiend she had become, and working with the Bellflower network, they smuggled her out of the city. She spent months with the firebrands in a remote corner of the desert, the Badwi nomads plying her addiction with pesh paste. For the first time in two decades, she could breathe free, and choose her own path. 7:47 AM . The Firebrands held many gods close to their heart, and she tried to pursue the faith of many of them. Calistria was too cruel, Milani too broad in purpose, Shelyn too soft, and Cayden Calien was too lush. Finally a Pathfinder from Avistan came through, a devout of Arazni, when she found her true home. A goddess who did not seek followers, but hated that she was needed in a place of divinity. She studied under this Pathfinder as she worked to wean herself off of Pesh. Daily drills, fencing, throwing blades, learning to use the bladed scarf, climbing, researching her goddess’ tenets and rites. Things changed when she felt she was ready to join the firebrands on a mission, an attempt to raid one of the last slave markets in Katapesh city. Their intel was bad. It was a sting. Her comrades fell in droves, and to Della’s horror, the Zephyr guard were reinforced with Kholo forces. Maybe it was panic, maybe the kholo had been the one to capture her, all she knew was she heard Arazni in her mind, demanding vengeance. For hours they fought, the Firebrands and the Zephyr guards, the tinny smells of blood, cordite and ozone flooding the noses of all involved. At the end of everything, it came down to Della and that oddly familiar Kholo. Her spells were all cast. Her rapier was broken. Her throwing blades were all thrown. Her bladed scarf was in tatters, her mane of black hair no longer hidden under her hijab. In a moment of desperation, she cried out to her goddess, demanding vengeance, and in a moment of divine intervention, she felt a weight in her rapier’s sheath. From that sheath, she drew a blade made of writhing blood, a boon from her goddess. She thanked her goddess by letting the blade fly from her hand. 7:47 AM . The blade struck true, but the beastly Kholo was not felled. But Arazni’s will was unyielding. In an instant, the blade was back in her hand. She threw again, and again, and again, until finally, her foe was done. Breathing heavily, exhausted and confused, she only had a moment to try and think of her next steps, before a convergence opened up around her, taking an entire city block with her. She knows not why she was called to Ao. But she trusts her goddess. And she knows she will free others from their bonds, and serve her lady, no matter where oppression hides. 7:50 AM @Sheet Checker @Trial Sheet Checker All Done! 8Plat: Baiwak9 Tarachi6 Della2 4/2/2026 8:02 PM Heyo, @Sheet Checker where am I in line? TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter V1triolic-Iwodoir 4, Weloh 2 4/2/2026 8:09 AM Name: Weloh-Ir Ancestry: Kobold Heritage: Custom Mixed-Halfling Class: Starlit Span Magus/Sniper Gunslinger Age: 18 8:10 AM Backstory: For as long as they can remember, Weloh-Ir was raised by a group of adventurers. The adventurers consisted of a human wizard, a halfling ranger, an orc gunslinger, and an elf fighter and smith; their names were Rergif, Ariwyn, Vrothu, Saevel respectively. Throughout their endeavours Weloh-Ir mostly hid in the back, hiding in the shadows of whoever was farthest from the adversaries. Over time, as Weloh-Ir got older the group started to teach them a variety of useful skills, but given their propensity to hide, Saevel decided against teaching them close quarters combat and instead taught them to strengthen their body. As the training continued Weloh-Ir progressively got better at both archery and marksmanship; however, their magic capabilities was lacking. This continued for a few years until Ariwyn got pregnant, the party disbanded, and Weloh-Ir was given a choice, to stay with Rergif and Ariwyn, or to continue adventuring with Vrothu and Saevel. Weloh-Ir ultimately decided to stay behind, and the group had a going away celebration for Vrothu and Saevel. During this party, the two gifted Weloh-Ir one of the guns that Vrothu used with some modifications made by Saevel to acommodate their small stature. The gun was at this point still almost twice the size of Weloh-Ir, but they still had time to grow into it. 8:10 AM And then several years passed, during those years, they continued training in magic and utilizing their new gun, while also spending time with their new brother. At some point during their training, Weloh-Ir miraculously managed to get a grasp of magic; however, it wasn't the normal way, they instead were only able to use their gun as a catalyst for their spells. Employing this newfound technique, Weloh-Ir was able to make breakneck improvements in there spellcasting capabilities, much to Rergif's delight. Then when Weloh-Ir turned 18, Rergif and Ariwyn described what happened all those years ago, that brought them to their group. They were on a mission to meet a kobold village in a nearby cave to assist them as members of the village were slowly disappearing, but when they got their, the village was empty. They scoured the village looking for clues of what happened, there were no signs of a struggle and it didn't seem like anyone planned to leave as there was still food on tables and the smoldering remains of fires. The only thing they could find was one solitary egg. They decided to take it upon themselves to raise the kobold inside, and that happened to be Weloh-Ir. They explained that the reason they told Weloh-Ir about this was so that they were ready to make the trek back their to get some closure. 8:10 AM After letting this knowledge sink in, Weloh-Ir decided that they would go to the remains of the village, and made way. Meeting Vrothu and Saevel on the way they journeyed forth, having not actually fought many monsters, Weloh-Ir was still timid during combat, but was able to at least be of some help using their newfound skills. Then they made it to the village, and entered cautiously, as it had been many years since they were all last there. But there was no cause for alarm, the village hadn't changed in years, outside of being weathered from age. As they were exploring Weloh-Ir saw a passageway that seemed to open up during the years left unattended, it was too small for Vrothu and Saevel to go through, so Weloh-Ir went in alone. But as they went through the tunnel they felt something strange, the walls seemed to move for a second, and when they looked back all they saw was darkness. They decided to press onward, and when they exited the tunnel they were outside, but they did not know where, and when they looked for the tunnel, it was gone, all that was left was rocks. Lost in this strange world, they decided that they would try to look for members of the kobold village, and maybe just maybe they would find a way back. 8:13 AM Okay @Sheet Checker this should be all good now Hectic- Strx12, Blmr9, Tgrfsh4 4/2/2026 1:33 PM Morafev @V1triolic-Iwodoir 4, Weloh 2 , I'll be reviewing your character sheet today 1:33 PM Art and Bio: 1:35 PM Inventory: starting total wealth exceeds the limit of 45 gp by 1gp (edited) 1:37 PM Feats: Magus isn't supposed to get a feat at level 1 (edited) Hectic- Strx12, Blmr9, Tgrfsh4 4/2/2026 1:45 PM Spell List: 1:52 PM Proficiencies: Arcana and stealth from classes, crafting and lore from background, survival from dedication. Blandit vestibulum convallis vivamus per di TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Jet [ Val 9 | Nox 10 | Ser 12 ] 2/26/2025 9:25 PM Name : Seraphina Ancestry : Elf Heritage : Lawbringer Nephilim Class : Cloistered Cleric | Life Oracle Age : 135 Backstory Born 135 years ago in the city of Kaelmont, Seraphina was marked from her earliest days by a celestial spark. As a Nephilim, she possessed a soft, radiant halo that hovered above her head; a silent testament to divine favor. This halo, which only grew more brilliant with her age, became a symbol of hope and healing to the people of Kaelmont. At a tender age, Seraphina was entrusted to the Church of Gruhastha, the revered institution dedicated to the deities teachings of compassion, resilience, and healing. The clergy, awed by her celestial aura and innate grace, believed she had been touched directly by divinity. Within the hallowed halls of the ancient cathedral, Seraphina was raised amongst healers and scholars, her days filled with prayer, study, and the constant care of the wounded and ailing. Despite her gentle demeanor and unwavering devotion, Seraphina carried a personal struggle—an almost pathological fear of grime and contamination. This germaphobia, perhaps a quirk of her ethereal nature or a side effect of years spent in the unsanitary conditions of plague-ridden wards, made her obsessively clean. Every tool in her healing kit was meticulously sterilized, and she insisted on performing even the smallest healing ritual with precision. This habit, though sometimes a source of ridicule among her more carefree peers, became part of her identity, a reminder that even divine touch must be balanced with human caution. On one of the days Seraphina was in charge of cleaning at the cathedral ( her favorite days, as she felt like she was the only priest there that took it seriously ), she heard an unexplainable voice. She couldn't tell what they where saying, or where it was coming from, only the sense that she was being beckoned. Without warning, she became bathed in a blinding light as she silently slipped out of existence, leaving nothing behind in the cold, marbled hall. When Seraphina opened her eyes, she was in a new place, and a new time. A place she would only later find out was called Ao. Done in foundry. The seed took many years to grow, but instead of growing into an ordinary plant, it grew Vaerus. Vaerus quickly found home in a community of humans that had previously been under his mother's control in previous generations. They instilled in him his cautious fear and loathing of his mother, and all fey at that fact. He learned to suspect her return at any time and methods to fight against monsters. In addition, he learned on his own how to control the magic that had been vital to his being and manifest it in the world.
